rationale: Y explicitly ties its findings to the actual resolution history (names commits d145581e/82a142ad matching Xunzhuo's real replies for the RGBA and dtype-promotion fixes) and does deeper, better-grounded investigation of the CI-failure claim by tracing that the AMD e2e lane does exercise the changed function via serving_video.py, contradicting a shallower dismissal; it also surfaces a genuinely novel, well-cited finding (2D frames now silently violate the documented (F,H,W,3) contract). X is more readable and gives concrete code-diff fixes (memory follow-up, scratch-buffer reuse) and catches the same dead-branch nit, but leans on several precise-sounding fuzz/benchmark numbers with no visible verification trail, which hurts trust in its grounding. Y's redundant near-duplicate 'stale test count' bullets and denser format cost it some actionability polish.
